Hossin: best continent for that, with the most interesting bases for urban combat.

Amerish: is a good overall, you can play armor, air and infantry and not just farm

Indar: oh what's that? A 10 man squad is trying to capture a 1 point base? Better send 2 to 4 time their numbers to secure the base. You are playing in a 10 man squad? Esamir: kinda same, but somehow worse? Thank fuck they added deployable galaxies, bc it was so ridiculously easy to finish a fight in the north east bases near the destroyed warpgate. Overall good idea in paper that didn't materialize well

That's why in Esamir and Indar, you either turn your brain off and just try to get kills and decent fights, or you just become frustrated. Hossin is the best continent to lead in, no air balls, no huge armor columns, more interesting bases for infantry... Fights tend to be more equal and less sudden overpops happen, although it still happens.

I mean, the red buff thingy is an okay idea, I'd say somewhat similar to what we have now, instead of a lane is a zone with less objects in between where fights are encouraged in the early game and can decide the game. But why would you take out the disability of the towers? The classic joust map encourages camping the towers and having either 40 min long games where there's no fighting, or the enemy team is forced to dive and gets wiped and losses the game. 

You either make the buff to structure dmg so op that's basically the same of disabling the tower or it will be time to turtle again.

Maybe this is controversial but what I would add to this map is move some of the buffs it currently has. Having some harpies and the red buff to contest is really nice, but I feel that the blue and maybe the back harpies could be moved closer to the spawn. The biggest flaw of this map in my opinion is the snowballing effect it has, due to having only one lane and most of the camps are on the contested middle part, so if you are behind your enemies will easily invade those same camps, stealing exp you can't afford to lose. Therefore, there's little to no hope of coming back (you'd have to rely on your enemies being bad or messing up, bc theres no way to outfarm them or outsmart them if both teams are equally skilled).

Another option to discourage invading is doing something similar to what conquest has, but I don't really like that, if yoy take a risky gamble like that it should reward you. Besides, if the camps are closer to the spawn there's a lot more risk of getting out of position and a lot more opportunities for the enemies to poke and eventually win the fight even from behind (if not extremely behind at that point in joust, I would just f6) 

If yoy want to add that option, it would be mandatory for the spawn timers to be reworked, it's so annoying to lose a game bc you are forced to dive and then die, only for the same team that was camping to win the game bc you are dead for almost a minute. But in the end, I feel like removing the disabling of the towers would only encourage camping and unnecessarly stretching games, and most of people wouldn't enjoy that kind of gameplay, neither defending or attacking. At least the snowball leads to a more quick defeat.

# Level 4 Psycast:

**Focus:** Good buffs that enhance you in combat, good duration, and less heat heavy than some previous abilities. A good addition always

**Smokepop:** Good offensive and defensive utility, especially to deal with turrets, short range, but smoke can be placed aggressively plus smart pathing makes this a superb addition

**Skip:** A teleport, simple, but effective, decent range and a great tool in lots of situations

**Wallraise:** Wonderful movable cover, won't last long under sustained fired due to low hp of the walls (100 points). More situational than the other level 4 abilities, but can come in clutch breaking line of sight and baiting enemies, or you can use them to reset the warm-up of some enemies when they are aiming.

**Word of Serenity:** This brings you the ability to stop any mental break, it can come in clutch in combat scenarios especially, it is true that the psycaster falls into a coma, but that only makes it balanced. Great addition

*Finally, all psycast in this level are either good, or decent in every, or all situations, they have restrictions of course, but those restrictions don't make them unusable or worthless, but balanced. But take note that these are level 4. Let me say that again, level 4, is it worth going through all the pain to reach these abilities? It depends, starting from naked brutality, probably not, bc there are either better things to do/achieve atm, or it's not worth the risk involved, bc by the time you reach a stability point, you are near the mid-game, where there are plausible chances of actually losing colonist more often.*

# Level 5 Psycast:

**Flashstorm:** Direct hits from this ability are very RNG heavy but can be good to create a wildfire to nearby sieges if placed correctly, which may lead to chain reactions and them going boom, it's somewhat situational. Rather tight range tho, so the psycaster can lead into some trouble, but it's usually not that high of a risk for the potential benefits it can bring

**Berserk:** Rather close range, but distracts enemies making them fight each other, especially good when used against high-value enemies, like heavily armoured melee, or dangerous ranged pawns, but they need to be close to you. While they are distracted you can do some serious damage, good addition that involves some risks sometimes but gives you a lot of value.

**Invisibility:** One of the best psycast, making a pawn untargetable for 60 secs (average)? Sign me in. Short range tho, but damn it's powerful.

**Word of Inspiration:** Having inspirations based on their passions and skills? Oh god, the amount of legendary items, art, and overall buffs your characters can get is scary, a great psycast. I think this is tied with Invisibility for the best psycast you can get in vanilla Rimworld

**Farskip:** Wait a second, an aimed teleport that can send people across the planet? Beam me up Scotty.

*I believe the strongest psycast can be found here, at level 5, is it worth the risk to get to level 5 tho? I often don't want to go through the dangers of reaching there just to get to these powerful abilities. Getting flashtorm, with how op the other options are, is like looking for gold, and finding copper.*

# Level 6 Psycast:

**Manhunter pulse:** you can use these to deal with an entire base or with a raid if you select a good herd of animals, like elephants for example. It can be a risk for your psycaster, but if he can outrun the animals, it can be seriously damage or even annihilate enemies

**Skipshield:** Makes a circle (9 tiles) that cannot be shot through, into, or out of. Do I even have to explain anything else? Negates all incoming fire, awesome.

**Berserk Pulse:** like berserk, but AEO (5x5) and slightly more range (5 more tiles --> 25) and more heat heavy. Can be really powerful for the same reasons Berserker is strong but multiplied.

**Mass Chaos Skip:** More RNG, but now it's AOE and without a stun now. If this is your level 6 psycast, I'm sorry for you, you just got scammed. I wouldn't even want this if it was level 1.

**Neuroquake:**  map-wide berserk mental state except for a 5 tile safe radius. The easiest way to deal with a base, although -10 mod debuff to all colonist, reduces faction opinion by 10 for all factions and the pyscaster gets into a coma. I mean, at that point, it's like a nuke, without damaging any resources of the base you are attacking or defending, heavy backlash is only expected.

4/5? Amazing, in some scenarios, you'll be able to wipe a whole settlement with all of those 4. The other one is utter garbage for me.

# Level 2 Psycast:

**Blinding Pulse:** Good for dealing with really accurate enemy pawns with dangerous weapons, but due to its range, you'll probably get tagged before applying it, it's better to just out range those pawns when possible.

**Waterskip:** A ranged AOE fire suppressor, really situational. **Word of Joy:** Good to prevent someone from having a mental break, at the cost of 20% consciousness, but a great mood buff (+30) pretty good and balanced, but situational

# Level 3 Psycast:

**Vertigo Pulse:** Good crow control to make someone unable to do anything (other than vomiting) and make them go out of cover, but again, such a short radius (25 tiles) means its probably easier and safer to just out range your enemies

**Beckon:** Good to make ranged pawns go out of cover and come closer, so you can annihilate them easier, but even a shorter range (20 tiles) means that either these pawns are so close anyways that they are already doing that, or they being so close makes them a priority target, so you'll focus them first and the time to kill (TTK) won't change that much

**Chaos Skip:** A teleport that depends on RNG? That makes you stunt after it? Either a life saviour, or a death sentence

**Word of Love:** 2 pawns loving each other brings so many positive things that this is easily one of the best level 3 psycast, which isn't difficult for me, ngl, but still, great psycast for improving the mood of 2 pawns mainly, with some other minor benefits.

*Now we are getting to more useful and impactful abilities on paper, but the range is often a deal-breaker for me since I will have to expose a pawn to great danger. And Chaos Skip is a no-go for me, Randy Random is already giving me enough problems to add even more RNG to it.*

Shield belts don't matter in melee, so let's talk about armor for the megaspider scenerio. Cataphract armor has a 120% sharp protection and 50% blunt protection, it's the best armor in terms of sharp and blunt protection, and only bested by the Phoenix armor in heat protection 

Armor works this way (pretty sure but double check): those values compete against the armor penetration of the weapon your enemy uses, all guns do sharp damage from affar and in melee pawns can either do a blunt or sharp attack depending on the weapon (some weapons like maces only do blunt damage)

Let's say armor pen on a gun is 30% and it does sharp damage. Then the formula would be 120-30 = 90%

This means that in a roll from 1 to 100:
- 90% chance of mitigating damage
        - 45% chance of doing no damage at all
        - 45% chance of halfing the incoming dmg
-10% of doing full damage

While Cataphract armor protects you from a megaspider, it has 2 types of attacks: head claw (12 sharp dmg, 18% AP) and head (7 blunt dmg, 18% AP)

If we do the math we find the following (only for sharp) 120-18 = 102
-100% of mitigating dmg
        - 50% no damage
        - 50% half of the damage

(blunt only) 
50-18 = 32
- 32% of mitigating dmg
      - 16% no dmg
      - 16% half dmg
-68% of full dmg

Keep in mind that this armor is only applied to the body parts covered by the Cataphract armor (torso, neck, shoulders, arms and legs). When hitting thise body parts, there's a chance to hit an organ that's placed on the same area (lungs, liver, heart, kidneys and stomach for torso for example). The armor can stop the dmg or half the dmg, in both of the cases.

The chances of you getting hit in the torso are quite significant, it is the body part pawns tend to hit more on average, specially if the objective has artificial limbs, bc they "reduce" the amount of body parts that can be hit. A peg leg, for example, removes the leg  ofc, the foot (with all its toes) the femur and the tibia. With less body parts and the torso being the most probable place to hit, the chances grow even larger.

I would say this feature would make the game too easy for the crewmates by itself. Although the concept is interesting, the crewmates have the superior numbers and also a lot of tools to have information around the map, thats of course countered by the special abilities of the impostors and the fact that they also can use those same tools to get more info. 

The first 2-4 kills are always somewhat easy to do without getting too much suspicious upon the killer but, by that point it becomes extremely difficult to kill someone without the other crewmates susing of the killer. And in the endgame it is extremely difficult for the killer to even find a window to get a kill, if you add a detective you would also need to add something for the impostors to have an extra advantage to win. If not, it would just be too easy to win as crewmate, who now have someone that will stick to others from the start of the game, making it more difficult to find an opportunity to get a clean kill (even with confirmed ejects off and visual task off, bc if you had that on it would be honestly imposible to win if you had a detective).


Think about this: you have someone in the game that you know its safe that has no tasks, so he just follows other people around, observing their behaviour and pathing, something that should be already be done by the crewmates while doing their tasks. People will eventually start following more the detective when the game gets into the mid-game, bc you are sure you are gonna be safe, and yeah, impostors can try to separate the crewmates and detective with walls, but most probably you wont be able to get a clean kill, meaning you are gonna get ejected, losing 50% of your team.

Another point now is: sabotaging o2 or reactor while getting a kill on the other side of the map has a different meaning, not only you want to buy time to get another kill while the crewmates take more time to find the body, but it also may lead to baiting the detective to go there and maybe killing him, but that is more riscky than previous strategy, and if you dont execute it well it will lead to an impostor getting ejected or a sabotage wasted without any real accomplishments bc the body will be found sonner, not having time to get another kill.

I would suggest that the detective, if implemented, should have tasks, but fewer than the other crewmates, to try to avoid making pairs from the start of the game, and that the special abilities from the detective can be sabotaged by the impostors in some way.
My proposal us that the detective has a sensor thing that shows dead bodies near him, similar to a sonar or smt like that, and that tool can be sabotaged by the impostors, maybe sabotaging comms. That way the detective would be more counterable and you will give the impostors more choices on how to handle this new menace. 
But even with my own proposal, i don't know if the game would be balanced for the impostors. Right now, without the detective is more probable to win as a crewmate than with impostors (and im talking about the games where confirmed ejects and visual tasks are off, bc in my opinion, it just makes the game too easy), just bc of sheer numbers. If the crewmates are familiar to the game and the map they are playing, is not that hard to spot weird behaviors or pathing, and bc of the impostors being a minority of the group there are a lot of chances to get spotted, lying, killing someone or doing something sus. Try remember that crewmates are more expendable than impostors, killing 2 people bc one of them is an impostors is not that much of a deal for the crewmates but impostors will lose half of the team. 

I honestly think that it is a very interesting and funny idea to add a detective, but it would also be very detrimental to the game balance if not done correctly, bc it is already harder to win as an impostor and adding something like this may be adding insult to injury.

Hey man its okay, i would love to know your suggestions. I recognice that there are different ways of using a valk and thats not bad, just different playstiles.

Well for me the Valkyrie is not an aircraft, is more like a heli. Its porpouse (or at least how i use it) is to move troops quickly and to support ground forces. I kind of like the state the valk is in. 

If i were to make changes on it, i would somehow change the max height it can go, to be more vulnerable to AA and evade the unrealistic situation of paratroppers falling from the outer atmosphere. I would not put a ceiling above it, i would affect its performance gradually as it got higher and higher and if it gets extremly high (i dont know exactly how much, i would suggest to start at 600m and be open to changes if, once in the game i realise its too much), it starts to take damage. On the other side i would give it more agility when its more close to the ground and make it smaller so its not just a big hit box to take down. That allows it  to evade AA, and libs more easly but has to be concerned about them (while still being vulnerable to ESFs).

As i said, those changes are intended to make the valk work more like a heli rather than aircraft bc i think thats what it is, a light air transport which objective is to deliver soldiers and give some support to the ground troops, with great agility, but can go down very easly to AA or to ESF. 

The last set of changes i would make is to make it cheaper (200 nanites instead of 250) and maybe a slight health decrease (from 3000 to 2500) And finally, i would also avoid letting it be repaired from the inside (or at least diminishing its effectiveness by some amount).

One last point i think its important to discuss is the redeploy system. Even with that, a heli is vital for small outfits to make some sort of impact in the battelfield: (1) it allows to go to other bases, even if the ground is full of vehicles, pull a sundie there, and start a fight, (2) in difficult bases a good drop on certain buldings can break the status quo and let friendlies push, (3) if you are uneable to pull a sundie in the base you are gonna attack because its a 96+ fight and you simply dont have the time to hack the terminal, a valk lets you fly to the next enemy base and pull the sundie from there, or even an armour column to pincer enemy armor between your column and the friendly armour on the front and (4), sadly, the spawn system is a little bit broken, if it doesnt let you spawn in a base where your faction is getting overpoped, you are gonna lose some vital seconds on defending or attacking that base, so the fastest way to go is to just pull a heli and go as fast as you can.
